hints: Look closely at the shape of the energy profile, it has two humps with a dip labelled Z in the middle. What type of substitution mechanism does that tell you about?
The carbon bonded to three other carbons is tertiary, so it first loses $\text{Cl}^-$ as $\text{Cl}^-$ to leave the carbon behind on its own at point Z.
Think about the difference between a partial charge in a transition state and a full charge on a real intermediate that sits in an energy valley.
walkthrough:
**Spot the type of halogenoalkane**

The reactive carbon is bonded to two ring carbons plus one $\text{CH}_3$ group. That is three carbons in total, so it is a tertiary chloroalkane.

Tertiary halogenoalkanes hydrolyse by $S_N1$, not $S_N2$.

**Read the energy profile**

The diagram shows two peaks with a valley at Z. That is the classic $S_N1$ profile.

$$\text{R-Cl} \rightarrow [\text{R}^+ + \text{Cl}^-] \rightarrow \text{R-OH}$$
Peak 1 is loss of $\text{Cl}^-$, valley Z is the carbocation intermediate, peak 2 is attack by $\text{OH}^-$.

**Find the charge at Z**

At Z the $\text{C-Cl}$ bond has fully broken heterolytically. Both bonding electrons have gone to chlorine:
$$\text{R-Cl} \rightarrow \text{R}^+ + \text{Cl}^-$$
The carbon has lost an electron pair, so it now has only 6 electrons and a full 1+ charge. It is a tertiary carbocation.

options.A: Incorrect. A 1- charge would mean the carbon gained electrons. Here the carbon loses the $\text{Cl}^-$ ion, so it loses electrons and becomes positive, not negative.
options.B: Incorrect. $\delta-$ means a small partial negative charge, as in a polar $\text{C}^{\delta+}-\text{Cl}^{\delta-}$ bond in the starting material. At Z the bond is fully broken and the carbon is electron deficient, so it cannot be negative.
options.C: Incorrect. $\delta+$ is only a partial charge found in a transition state at the top of an energy hump, for example in an $S_N2$ mechanism. Point Z is in a valley, so it is a stable intermediate with a full charge, not a transition state.
options.D: Correct. Point Z is the carbocation intermediate of the $S_N1$ reaction. After $\text{Cl}^-$ leaves, the tertiary carbon is left with a full 1+ charge.
